Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; I can pull specific CAIQ/SIG snippets afterwards.

- Geo-lockdown (EU only): Yes — when you select the EU hosting option we will ensure primary storage, backups, and snapshot replication remain within EU regions that you select. Automated failover is configurable — by default we keep failover within the same geographic region grouping; cross-region failover is only enabled with an account-level op in our console and requires explicit acceptance. In short: EU-only is supported and will not replicate to the US unless you opt into cross-region DR.

- Private connectivity (Privatelink): Our privatelink endpoint is a managed endpoint in Redwood's VPC that establishes a private, tenant-specific tunnel into your VPC via a customer-managed peering attachment. Minimum required CIDR blocks: we recommend a /28 for the peering subnet (we will provide exact ranges scoped per account). Maintenance windows for peering changes are scheduled in coordination with your network team; we do not make rolling changes without notice.

- KMS & tenant isolation: We use tenant-scoped KMS keys for customer workloads (separate key material per tenant) in the EU region. Backups are encrypted with the same region-specific KMS material. I'll attach a short SOC2/SIG extract and our deployment matrix that shows the per-region isolation lanes.

Next steps / action items:
- I've attached: redwood-deploy-matrix.csv (region mapping), privatelink-datasheet.pdf (network checklist), soc2-summary.txt (SOC2 excerpt).
- Marissa — could you confirm the standard CIDR allocations we propose for Medivault and add any extra notes on scheduled peering ops?
- Mina — can you confirm the KMS partitioning note (separate key per tenant) and whether backups are physically written to EU-only storage for the EU account configuration?

Sara, if it's useful I can also produce a short one-page attestation letter you can attach to procurement.

Best,
